{{Lowercase title}}
In [[mathematics]], an '''ω-bounded space''' is a [[topological space]] in which the [[closure (topology)|closure]] of every [[countable set|countable subset]] is [[compact space|compact]]. More generally, if ''P'' is some property of subspaces, then a ''P''-bounded space is one in which every subspace with property ''P'' has compact closure.

Every compact space is ω-bounded, and every ω-bounded space is [[countably compact]]. The [[long line (topology)|long line]] is ω-bounded but not compact.

The [[bagpipe theorem]] describes the ω-bounded surfaces.
